Exposure by kernel

Source: R/sep.R
kerexp.Rd

The kernel-weighted density of sources at each receptor, sum_j w_j K(d_ij / h) / h^2, with the bivariate normal kernel exp(-u^2 / 2) / (2 pi) or the quartic kernel 3 / pi (1 - u^2)^2 (for u < 1, 0 beyond) of Bailey and Gatrell (1995). Planar coordinates.

Usage

kerexp(x, y = NULL, src, h, w = NULL, kern = "gaussian")

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

src

The sources: a matrix or data frame of two coordinate columns, as x.

h

The bandwidth: one positive number.

w

NULL for a weight of 1 per source, or one weight from 0 per source.

kern

"gaussian" or "quartic".

Value

A numeric vector, one value per receptor.

References

Bailey, T. C. and Gatrell, A. C. (1995). Interactive Spatial Data Analysis. Longman, Harlow.

See also

Other spatial epidemiology: bayout(), bufexp(), bym2sc(), ecolrg(), evfilt(), lerprc(), sfrail(), spbias(), spsir()

Examples

kerexp(rbind(c(0.2, 0.3)), src = rbind(c(0.25, 0.35), c(0.6, 0.8)),
       h = 0.5, kern = "quartic")
#> [1] 3.668458
